title: One command surface (PI-04)
summary: Also known as PI-04. Commands to run and validate the BPM Platform stack were duplicated across README.md, CLAUDE.md, docs/guides/backend_developer_guide.md, docs/guides/test_developer_guide.md, and docs/guides/test_infrastructure_guide.md, forked between bash and PowerShell forms, with every agent hand-assembling env vars plus the raw command. TEST-RUNNER's service pre-check was prose describing a manual, non-blocking check rather than a wait, which is where INFRA_BLOCK round-trips between ORCH and BACKEND-DEV came from.

design_decision.script: Built make.ps1 at the repo root (PowerShell, this repo's primary environment) with exactly the subcommands named in the issue blueprint: up, migrate, test, test-live, e2e, check, plus help/no-args. up runs docker compose up -d then polls each service's Docker health status (reusing the healthchecks already in docker-compose.yml/docker-compose.override.yml) up to 10x. migrate/test-live source BPM_DB_URL/BPM_TEST_DB_URL from .env via the script's own dotenv loader rather than requiring the caller to export them. test-live waits for Postgres+Keycloak (same readiness logic as up) before running zig build test-integration — this is what makes 'service not up' stop being an agent-visible failure per the issue's done-when criterion.
design_decision.check_scoping: PI-03 (zig build check, a real build-graph-integrated gate combining zig fmt --check + build + error-set grep) is a SEPARATE, still-open issue (GH-293) — verified directly: gh issue view 293 --json state returned OPEN, and grep -n 'b.step("check"' build.zig found no such step. Implementing PI-03's gate logic here would be uncoordinated scope creep on an already-substantial MAJOR issue. make.ps1 check is built as option (a) from the issue brief: an explicitly-labelled interim stand-in running exactly the two commands CLAUDE.md's BACKEND-DEV section already mandates before self-review (zig build + an error-set grep on its output), with every output line prefixed to make clear this is not PI-03's real gate. zig fmt --check src/ was tried and dropped: it reports 225 pre-existing files as unformatted repo-wide (unrelated to this change, and zig fmt was never part of CLAUDE.md's mandated self-review checklist), so including it would make the interim stand-in fail for reasons unrelated to whatever change is being validated.
design_decision.powershell_5_1_finding: An early draft set $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop' at the top of the script. This was wrong: zig build test and other native tools write normal progress/advisory text to stderr on a SUCCESSFUL run, and PowerShell 5.1's NativeCommandError wrapping (triggered by 'Stop') turns that stderr traffic into a terminating error even though the process's own exit code is 0. Fixed by removing the blanket ErrorActionPreference and judging every native command exclusively by $LASTEXITCODE. Also confirmed a related quirk: invoking the script itself with an outer 2>&1 (e.g. '.\make.ps1 test 2>&1') reproduces the same wrapping one layer up in the caller's shell — this is a PowerShell 5.1 characteristic, not a script defect (confirmed by running the same command with and without the outer redirection).
design_decision.docs_updated: README.md, CLAUDE.md, docs/guides/backend_developer_guide.md, docs/guides/test_developer_guide.md, docs/guides/test_infrastructure_guide.md were each grepped for the specific raw commands (zig build migrate, zig build test-integration, docker-compose up -d/docker compose up -d, zig build test, npx playwright test) and updated to show the make.ps1 form as primary, with the raw form kept alongside (not deleted) where it appears inside a hard-gate instruction agents currently rely on for literal command text (CLAUDE.md's ADHOC BACKEND-DEV task template, TEST-RUNNER pre-check, BACKEND-DEV Allowed-commands list). .github/agents/*.agent.md and .github/instructions/*.instructions.md were deliberately NOT touched — they are a separate instruction layer not named in the issue's affected-files list (README.md, CLAUDE.md, docs/guides/), and tools/lint_agent_docs.py does not check CLAUDE.md itself (only the per-agent files against docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md), so this PR does not trip that linter by leaving them unchanged. Touching 8 more per-agent files would have meaningfully exceeded Effort: S.

evidence.make_ps1_up: Ran ./make.ps1 up against this workspace's real containers (r-co-2-db-1, r-co-2-db_test-1, r-co-2-keycloak-1, r-co-2-keycloak_gateway-1, already healthy): readiness attempt 1/10 reported all four healthy, script exited 0.
evidence.make_ps1_migrate: Ran ./make.ps1 migrate against this workspace's real BPM_DB_URL (port 5452): applied one pending migration (1143_iss0646_fix_gbl133_ledger_poisoning.sql), exited 0.
evidence.make_ps1_test: Ran ./make.ps1 test (zig build test, unit only): completed with the ISS-602 differential corpus and iss0173-orphan test blocks passing as expected, exit 0 (confirmed by running the underlying zig build test directly with RAW_EXIT=0, since PowerShell 5.1's outer 2>&1 wrapping made $LASTEXITCODE misleading when captured through this tool's own redirection — documented in src/design/unified-command-surface.md).
evidence.make_ps1_check: Ran ./make.ps1 check after dropping the zig fmt --check step: zig build succeeded, no 'error set' text in output, script printed 'PASSED (interim stand-in — not the real PI-03 gate; see GH-293)' and exited 0.
evidence.make_ps1_test_live: Ran ./make.ps1 test-live: readiness wait passed immediately at attempt 1/10 (services already healthy) and correctly proceeded straight to zig build test-integration with BPM_TEST_DB_URL sourced from .env — confirming the readiness-wait/env-sourcing logic this issue is actually about works correctly. The aggregate test-integration run itself then surfaced a large volume of pre-existing advisory-lock contention (many unrelated test files — env01, iss101, iss107, iss601, exp103, onboarding_realm_guard, etc. — all failing at the same runMigrations/acquireIntegrationLock choke point on bpm_test_migrations_public; confirmed via psql pg_stat_activity showing 10+ concurrent SELECT pg_advisory_lock(...) callers queued simultaneously). Cross-checked against git log: this workspace has an extensive, active, ongoing history of exactly this class of test-integration lock/race issue under active remediation by prior WF-03 runs unrelated to this one (ISS-0659/GH-681 'extend advisory lock to all 31 self-managed-pool binaries', ISS-0658, ISS-0655, ISS-0654, ISS-0652, ISS-0651, ISS-0646 among the last ~20 commits touching this exact area) — this is pre-existing, already-tracked infrastructure flakiness in the full aggregate suite, not something make.ps1 introduced or modified (make.ps1 only wraps the existing zig build test-integration invocation; it does not alter test code, fixtures, or locking). Per this task's own explicit guidance to use judgment on whether running the full aggregate suite is warranted versus trusting zig build test-integration itself (since that suite is not what this change touches), the background run was stopped once the readiness-wait/dispatch behavior was confirmed correct, rather than waiting out an already-known-flaky multi-hundred-binary suite for a result unrelated to this issue's scope. No new GH issue was filed for this contention since it is already covered by ISS-0659/GH-681 and its lineage.
evidence.e2e_syntax_check: cd web && npm run test:e2e:list enumerated 195 tests across 33 spec files with no config errors, confirming make.ps1 e2e's underlying invocation (npm run test:e2e from web/) is syntactically correct.
evidence.zig_build_overall: zig build (full build, not just make.ps1 check's subset) exits 0.
evidence.lint_agent_docs: .venv/Scripts/python.exe tools/lint_agent_docs.py — '34 agent files checked — 0 BLOCKER, 0 MAJOR, 0 MINOR', exit 0.
evidence.raw_command_sweep: grep -n for zig build migrate / zig build test-integration / docker-compose up -d / docker compose up -d / npx playwright test across README.md, CLAUDE.md, and all three docs/guides/*.md files confirmed every remaining raw-command site now has a make.ps1 reference immediately adjacent, is an intentionally-kept 'what it expands to' form, or is unrelated prose (e.g. a migrationOrder() cross-reference) rather than an instruction restating the command.

resolution: 1) make.ps1 (new, repo root): PowerShell script with up/migrate/test/test-live/e2e/check/help subcommands, a .env loader, and shared Docker-health-based readiness polling. 2) README.md: Quick start steps 1-2 and the Development commands table now show make.ps1 as primary with raw forms kept underneath. 3) CLAUDE.md: BACKEND-DEV Validate step, Allowed-commands list, ORCH's INFRA_BLOCK ADHOC task template, TEST-RUNNER's backend-services pre-check, and FRONTEND-DEV's e2e validate step now reference make.ps1 alongside the existing raw forms. 4) docs/guides/backend_developer_guide.md: Bootstrap-test-database section and Build Commands Reference table updated. 5) docs/guides/test_developer_guide.md: CI Integration Notes step list and TEST-RUNNER pre-flight checklist updated. 6) docs/guides/test_infrastructure_guide.md: INV-TI-1 verification command, manual-migrate example, and Green-Main-Gate Step 00a procedure updated. 7) src/design/unified-command-surface.md (new): Type E design note covering what was built, the check scoping decision, the PowerShell 5.1 ErrorActionPreference finding, and what was deliberately left unchanged. 8) docs/issues/ISS-0079.json (this file).
prevention: When a backlog entry names a subcommand as 'X's gate' but X is tracked as a separate, still-open issue, verify the other issue's actual state (gh issue view --json state, plus a direct grep for the artefact it would produce) before either implementing it here or silently omitting it — this issue's PI-04/PI-03 split is the second time in this same workspace session that a blueprint referenced a not-yet-built neighboring gate (see ISS-0080/PI-05, ISS-0082/PI-07 for the sibling pattern of scoping precisely against backlog entries). When wrapping native commands (zig, npm, docker) in a PowerShell script, never set $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop' at the top — many native tools write normal, successful-run output to stderr, and PowerShell 5.1 turns that into a terminating NativeCommandError regardless of the process's real exit code; judge every native command by $LASTEXITCODE instead, and be aware that testing a script via an outer '... 2>&1' redirection can reproduce the same misleading wrapping one layer up even when the script itself is correct.
